source.title: Understanding Image Representations by Measuring Their Equivariance and Equivalence

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; some mathematical notation and names are affected by text-extraction formatting.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether different CNN representations are interchangeable using learned stitching layers and downstream classification performance, a conceptual test of representation equivalence.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the stitched-network equivalence experiments in Section 3.3 and Table 4. Results on image equivariance and structured-output regression do not measure the claim versions. The paper also reports that identity stitching gives top-1 error greater than 99%; this is an aggregate comparator, not a result for each source model and layer.
record.test_reason: Learned stitching layers swap early layers of IMNET, PLCS and PLCS-H into ALEXN. ILSVRC12 top-1 error then shows whether a simple linear map makes the representations interchangeable (V4). The comparison across same-data and different-data sources and across depth bears on V7's incompleteness and shared-data parts.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the first several CNN layers are interchangeable, and hence equivalent, across different networks and training data via learned stitching. Deeper layers, especially Conv5, are less compatible and more task-specific, yet still far better than chance.
record.recipe_differences: Tests equivalence using learned stitching layers and downstream ImageNet classification performance; it does not use a scale-based representation-similarity measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Compatibility varies by stitched layer and source network/training dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Within ALEXN, learned linear maps compensate image flips, rotations and rescaling; the number of invariant channels varies by layer (Tables 2-3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CNN layer representations are linearly equivariant to geometric transforms, with layer-dependent invariance.

record.problems: The equivalence evidence is limited to three source CNNs and one downstream classification task. Performance after stitching is an indirect measure of representational equivalence; no uncertainty estimates are stated, and the identity-map error is only an aggregate text statement.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 also reports top-5 errors; they are not separately extracted because the row set records the main top-1 metric, and the paper does not use the two metrics to describe a differing conclusion.

untested.parts: No sweep over model scale or capability.
No same-architecture, different-seed comparison. IMNET and ALEXN share data but differ slightly in structure, and per-unit correspondence is not analysed.
Only learned linear stitching between vision CNNs is tested, with a task loss on ILSVRC12. Relative representations, mapping without paired data, and cross-modal mapping are untested.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits are compared across models.
No comparison of similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of a plateau with scale or of a common-world-model explanation. The data effect rests on only three source networks.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The stitching layers are trained with the ILSVRC12 task loss and evaluated with the fixed ALEXN head, so compatibility for the Places-trained source is also judged on ImageNet. No uncertainty is reported. Top-5 errors are declared left out and follow the same pattern.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or comparison of alignment against model size or capability.
No vision-language or paired image-caption representation comparison.
The study does not compare models trained from different initializations of the same architecture.
Tests learned stitching between vision CNNs on a classification task; does not test relative representations, mapping without paired task data, or cross-modal mappings.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Does not compare similarity metrics or settings such as neighbour counts, nor test out-of-distribution inputs.

The study compares models trained on different datasets but does not establish that shared data or objectives cause compatibility, test a scale-related plateau, or distinguish a common world model from other explanations.

tranche.reason: Learned linear stitching and downstream classification test representation interchangeability using a different method from scale-based representation-similarity measurements.

source_check.notes: Stitching measures retained ILSVRC12 classification performance, not complete representational identity. Training-data differences are associated with compatibility but are not isolated causally; plateauing and a common model of reality are untested.
